summary: Idle-tick rotation stamps the winner BEFORE dispatch, but step1_triage is the only candidate whose body sits after three unconditional head-decoupled lanes — two of which JUMP TO end. When one of them dispatches, PO triage is skipped and its rotation turn is consumed anyway.

payload.what_happened: Rotation selected step1_triage (oldest stamp, 01:16:34Z). Its stamp was advanced to 05:09Z immediately, per spec (unconditional, before dispatch). Control flow then reached Review-Lane QA-Drain Head-Decoupled, which claimed a row and dispatched qa, then executed its documented `JUMP TO end   # a batch was dispatched this tick; do not also fall through to Step 1/PO triage same tick`. PO triage never ran. step1_triage went from oldest stamp to newest without doing any work.

cost_this_tick.includes: the P0 resolver hot/cold divergence escalation (dedup_key resolver:effective_next_agent|hot-cold-next_agent-divergence) drained into the inbox this same tick
cost_this_tick.deferral: step1_triage cannot be re-selected until the other 5 candidates have each had a turn — up to 6 idle ticks, roughly 3 hours at the 7,37 cadence

structural_asymmetry.claim: step1_triage is the ONLY one of the 6 rotation candidates exposed to this. The other 5 are structurally immune.
structural_asymmetry.why: The 5 other candidates bodies all sit BEFORE the session gate (930), so they execute before any head-decoupled lane can jump to end. step1_triage has no body at the rotation site at all — the spec says so explicitly (its actual dispatch stays at line 1139 because it needs pendingSignals/reports gathered upstream and must stay reachable from Step 0b busy-tick bypass paths). That placement puts it downstream of ILC and QA-Drain-HD, both of which JUMP TO end on a successful dispatch.

payload.why_the_spec_does_not_cover_this: The no-same-tick-cascade rationale at line 573 addresses the case where $SELECTED s OWN gate/promote/claim is a genuine no-op — there the burned turn is intentional and harmless. It does not contemplate $SELECTED being PREEMPTED by a different, unconditional lane after its stamp was already consumed. The stamp-before-dispatch choice is separately well-argued (single call site vs five duplicated writes at each lane exit), so the defect is the interaction, not either decision alone.
payload.frequency_expectation: Not rare. review[] is chronically non-empty (26 rows at time of writing), so QA-Drain-HD has work on most ticks. Any tick where step1_triage wins rotation AND QA-Drain-HD or ILC dispatches will burn the triage turn. That biases the inbox toward growing rather than draining.
asks: Decide whether a preempting head-decoupled dispatch should roll back (or not consume) the selected candidates rotation stamp. Rolling back only in the preemption case preserves the existing no-op-turn semantics untouched.

Alternatively, exempt step1_triage from the JUMP TO end of ILC/QA-Drain-HD, since it neither writes .head nor competes for the WIP slot — the stated reason those lanes jump to end is to avoid a same-tick cascade among dispatching lanes, which PO triage is not.

Either way, add a regression assertion to scripts/audits/devteam-dispatch-gate-satisfiability.sh: when $SELECTED == step1_triage and QA-Drain-HD dispatches, PO triage must still be reachable OR the stamp must not have advanced.
payload.router_note: Router does not author task rows. Filed as a signal for architect/PO triage. Router followed the flow as written this tick (dispatched qa, skipped Step 1) rather than improvising around the documented JUMP TO end.
